# The package server on GitHub

This page is for developers who want to understand, copy or contribute to the package server. It explains the
repository [se7enxweb/exponential.packages.exponential.earth](https://github.com/se7enxweb/exponential.packages.exponential.earth),
how GitHub turns it into <https://exponential.packages.exponential.earth/>, and what each file outside the release
folders is for. Repository facts were read with `gh api` (read only) on 2026-10-18.

## The repository

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Name | `se7enxweb/exponential.packages.exponential.earth` |
| Visibility | public |
| Default branch | `master` |
| Homepage | <https://exponential.packages.exponential.earth/> |
| Fork of | `ezpublishlegacy/packages.ezpublishlegacy.com`, the 2014 mirror ([History](history-of-the-package-server.md)) |
| Size | about 2.5 GB with its history (the GitHub API reports 2,520,299 KB) |
| Issues | enabled |
| Commits | 341 (to 2026-10-16) |

The tree:

```text
.github/FUNDING.yml
.github/workflows/workflow.yml
CNAME
README.md
crossdomain.xml
exponential/6.0/<version>/index.xml
exponential/6.0/<version>/<name>.ezpkg
exponential/6.0/<version>/thumbnails/<name>.png
```

> **Tip**
> The repository is large because every `.ezpkg` of every release is kept in its history. For reading, clone it
> without blobs: `git clone --filter=blob:none https://github.com/se7enxweb/exponential.packages.exponential.earth.git`,
> then use `git log` and `git ls-tree -r -l HEAD`; Git fetches a file's content only when you open it.

## From push to web site

| Step | What happens |
|---|---|
| 1 | A commit is pushed to `master` (directly or by merging a pull request) |
| 2 | The workflow `main` starts (`on: [push]`) |
| 3 | Job `pages-directory-listing` checks out `master`, writes an `index.html` into every folder and uploads the whole tree as the Pages artifact |
| 4 | Job `deploy` publishes that artifact to the `github-pages` environment |
| 5 | GitHub Pages serves it under the custom domain from `CNAME`, HTTPS enforced |

The Pages settings, as the API reports them: build type `workflow` (not a branch), source branch `master`, custom
domain `exponential.packages.exponential.earth`, HTTPS enforced. The workflow has run 150 times; the
runs are listed under [Actions](https://github.com/se7enxweb/exponential.packages.exponential.earth/actions).

> **Note**
> While a deployment runs, the server can answer with errors for a few minutes. This is why the setup wizard retries
> a failed download ([When the package server cannot be reached](when-the-package-server-cannot-be-reached.md)).

## The workflow file

`.github/workflows/workflow.yml`, shortened to its working lines:

```yaml
name: main
on: [push]

concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  pages-directory-listing:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
        with:
          ref: master
      - uses: jayanta525/github-pages-directory-listing@main
        with:
          FOLDER: .
      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        with:
          path: '.'

  deploy:
    needs: pages-directory-listing
    permissions:
      pages: write
      id-token: write
    environment:
      name: github-pages
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4
```

| Part | Why |
|---|---|
| `concurrency: group: pages`, `cancel-in-progress: false` | One deployment at a time. Its comment: "A push that arrives while a deployment runs waits for it, and only the newest waiting push deploys; each deployment publishes the whole tree as of its commit, so nothing is lost when an older waiting one is skipped." Added on 2026-10-12, when packages pushed one after another made each other's deployments fail |
| `ref: master` | Always deploys the branch, whatever ref was pushed |
| `FOLDER: .` | Listing pages for the whole tree, from the top |
| `path: '.'` | The whole checkout is the site |
| `permissions` | The deploy job may write to Pages and request an OIDC token, which `deploy-pages` needs |

The real file also has steps that print `ls -al` and `du -sh .`, to see the size of the artifact in the log.

## The directory listing action

[jayanta525/github-pages-directory-listing](https://github.com/jayanta525/github-pages-directory-listing) generates
the "Index of /..." page for each folder. What the pages look like is described in
[Browsing the package server in a browser](browsing-the-package-server-in-a-browser.md). Before 2023-12-24 the
server used a JavaScript file browser in a hand-made `index.html`; it was replaced by this action.

## CNAME

`CNAME` holds one line, the host name GitHub Pages answers to:

```text
exponential.packages.exponential.earth
```

It has had this value since 2025-08-13. Changing it moves the site to another host name; every installation whose
`RemotePackagesIndexURL` names the old one would then depend on a redirect. Do not change it in a pull request.

## FUNDING.yml

`.github/FUNDING.yml` makes GitHub show a **Sponsor** button on the repository. It names GitHub Sponsors for the
`se7enxweb` organization, Patreon, and custom links to PayPal, Venmo, Cash App and <https://se7enx.com>. It was created
on 2023-12-24. It has no effect on the web site. See [Who is the Exponential Foundation?](../../who-is-the-exponential-foundation.md)
for how the project is funded.

## crossdomain.xml and README.md

- `crossdomain.xml` is a cross-domain policy that allows access from any domain (`<allow-access-from domain="*"/>`).
  It came with the 2014 mirror; nothing in Exponential reads it.
- `README.md` names the server ("Package server for Exponential 6."), the date of its last update, and links to the
  project, the package server, the documentation, the community and the vendor. It is served as a file of the site
  and shown on the repository's front page.

## Copying the setup for your own server

The same three things make any repository a package server: release folders with an `index.xml` and the packages, a
Pages workflow like the one above, and, if you want your own host name, a `CNAME` file and a DNS record for it. See
[Running your own package server](../your-own/running-your-own-package-server.md). For a package that everyone
should get, a pull request to this repository is the better way:
[Contribute your site package](../contribute-your-site-package.md).
